title: An ad campaign causes a spike in demand

request.title: Autumn campaign: demand far above plan
request.instructions: Our autumn campaign (Herbstzauber) works almost too well: order intake is far above plan and several new sales orders have no production order yet. Make sure we can deliver what we sold without burning out the factories. Decide whether the campaign has to be throttled (do not stop it completely, we still want the sales), ask Cora to plan the new orders, Max to secure capacity, and Lara to secure the material.

Cora.text:
# Planning autumn bundles can still end late

Rule: A healthy-looking factory queue and material projection do not guarantee that a large unplanned autumn bundle will finish on time; verify the post-change late-order KPI and material-shortage projection before treating the plan as sufficient.

Applies when: Several confirmed but unplanned sales orders are added together during a campaign spike and no extra capacity lever is booked.

Evidence: task `task-a2a-868119cc-9a29-4881-a984-46c0d33a5118`, KPI before `lateOrders=0`, `sofasLate=0`, `unplannedOrders=8` -> after `lateOrders=8`, `sofasLate=970`, `unplannedOrders=0`, `materialShortages={"FOAM-HR35":"production held back from 2026-11-12"}`. Reconfirmed in task `task-a2a-7f936446-e11a-49a9-b9a4-49c7504d3147`, KPI before `lateOrders=0`, `sofasLate=0`, `unplannedOrders=8` -> after `lateOrders=8`, `sofasLate=970`, `unplannedOrders=0`, `materialShortages={"FOAM-HR35":"production held back from 2026-11-11"}`. Reconfirmed again in task `task-a2a-0a7827d1-1a0c-4b1b-a2c9-ebe93ff49b49`, KPI before `lateOrders=0`, `sofasLate=0`, `unplannedOrders=8` -> after `lateOrders=8`, `sofasLate=970`, `unplannedOrders=0`, `materialShortages={"FOAM-HR35":"production held back from 2026-11-12"}`.

# North replan after spindle motor delivery

Rule: When `N-CUT-1` is down for the spindle motor replacement, replan only the North orders that are already late if moving additional work would increase the KPI.

Applies when: A North machine outage is tied to `MT-001` and the required part is already secured with a known arrival date.

Evidence: task `task-a2a-7869e423-a373-4844-a249-0c76c2b9dffa`, KPI before `lateOrders=5`, `sofasLate=520`, `lateOrdersCustomerNotInformed=5` -> after `lateOrders=2`, `sofasLate=220`, `lateOrdersCustomerNotInformed=2`.

- [Log](log.md): append-only session notes for durable company learnings.
- [Planning autumn bundles can still end late](lessons/autumn-bundle-late-even-with-capacity.md): unplanned bundles can still leave all orders late even when current capacity and stock look healthy.
- [North replan after spindle motor delivery](lessons/north-replan-spindle-motor.md): what we learned about re-planning North orders after the spindle motor arrives.

# Goal
Secure additional production capacity for the Herbstzauber backlog only if the live ERP shows a real capacity need. The current facts do not show a capacity bottleneck: both factories are at 40 sofas/day for the next 10 workdays, and the remaining lateness is driven by the FOAM-HR35 shortage, not by factory capacity.

# Inputs
- Live ERP overview: F-NORTH and F-SOUTH both show 40 sofas/day for the next 10 workdays; alerts are empty; KPI is `lateOrders=8`, `sofasLate=970`, `lateOrdersCustomerNotInformed=8`, `materialShortages=FOAM-HR35 from 2026-11-12`, `costOfMeasuresEur=0`.
- Late production orders are `PRD-4218`..`PRD-4225`; the backlog is already split across both factories, and several orders are blocked by `FOAM-HR35` rather than by labor capacity.
- Capacity-lever wiki rule: choose by KPI, not by machine/worker status; overtime tops out at 48 sofas/day and temporary workers start 3 workdays after the request.
- What-if checks: overtime for F-NORTH or F-SOUTH from `2026-10-05` to `2026-10-23` would each cost EUR 21,000, keep `lateOrders=8` and `sofasLate=970`, and add a new `BEAM-PINE-80` shortage.
- Company wiki read: `index.md`, `protocols/ordered-delegation.md`, `rules/capacity-levers.md`, `rules/customer-notices.md`.

# Steps
1. Do not book any overtime or temporary workers, because the simulated capacity packages do not improve lateness and only add cost and a new material shortage.
2. Report the live capacity state unchanged: both factories remain at 40 sofas/day for the next 10 workdays, with no new capacity measures booked.
3. If the approver later wants a different tradeoff, re-run `erp__simulate_change` with a combined capacity package before any execute step; no follow-up delegation is needed for the current decision.

# Outputs
- `.agent/plans/task-a2a-9b2f8658-9367-4a9a-9cd3-05f85676bd71.md`
- `.agent/summaries/task-a2a-9b2f8658-9367-4a9a-9cd3-05f85676bd71_plan_1.md`

# Risks and open questions
- The backlog remains late because of the FOAM-HR35 shortage; capacity booking cannot solve that bottleneck by itself.
- If later ERP facts show a separate labor bottleneck, the smallest effective mix should be re-evaluated with `erp__simulate_change` before booking anything.

# Goal
Re-plan the 8 confirmed but unplanned Herbstzauber sales orders in the shared ERP state so they are all turned into production orders without disturbing the existing confirmed production orders or their priorities. Protect the tier-A customers first (`SO-2303`, `SO-2304`), keep the two-factory setup, and report the resulting production orders with the ERP completion and delivery dates plus any orders that remain late.

# Inputs
- ERP overview now: `lateOrders=0`, `sofasLate=0`, `unplannedOrders=8`, `materialShortages={}`.
- The unplanned orders are `SO-2301..SO-2308` with total quantity `970` sofas.
- Both factories show `40 sofas/day` for each of the next 10 workdays; all machines are running and both factories have 2 regular workers.
- Current production queue is empty, so there are no existing production priorities to disturb.
- Material projections are clean for the relevant SKUs: `BEAM-PINE-80`, `FAB-OAT-01`, and `FOAM-HR35` all show no shortage within 70 workdays.
- Wiki: `index.md`, `protocols/handoffs.md`, `protocols/ordered-delegation.md`, `rules/capacity-levers.md`, `rules/customer-notices.md`, `company/overview.md`, `lessons/autumn-bundle-late-even-with-capacity.md`, `lessons/north-replan-spindle-motor.md`. Takeaway: healthy-looking capacity does not guarantee on-time delivery, so the plan must be validated against the KPI after replanning.

# Steps
1. Create all 8 sales orders as production orders with priority `6` so they do not displace existing priority-5 work.
2. Use the simulator-supported balanced split that keeps the tier-A orders first and spreads the backlog across both factories: create `SO-2303`, `SO-2301`, `SO-2305`, `SO-2307` in `F-NORTH`, and `SO-2304`, `SO-2302`, `SO-2306`, `SO-2308` in `F-SOUTH`, all at priority `6`.
3. After the creates, re-read the live production orders (`lateOnly=true`) to capture which of the newly planned orders are still late and record the ERP-computed completion and delivery dates for the report.
4. Accept that the simulator showed this bundle still leaves all 8 orders late and introduces no material shortage; do not add capacity levers in this step because they do not remove the lateness in the tested bundles.

# Outputs
- `.agent/plans/task-a2a-0a7827d1-1a0c-4b1b-a2c9-ebe93ff49b49.md`
- `.agent/summaries/task-a2a-0a7827d1-1a0c-4b1b-a2c9-ebe93ff49b49_plan_1.md`
- In the execution report: the new production order ids, their ERP completion/delivery dates, and the final `lateOrders` / `sofasLate` / `unplannedOrders` KPI.

# Risks and open questions
- The simulator showed no 8-order split that makes the KPI clean; the chosen bundle still leaves all 8 orders late, so approval must accept that outcome or request a different tradeoff.
- Some later orders may not get finite completion dates in the first simulation horizon, so the live ERP must be re-read after execution.
- Material is currently fine, but this assumes no other live change happens before execution.

# Goal
Keep the Herbstzauber demand spike deliverable without stopping sales entirely. The current issue is 8 unplanned sales orders totaling 970 sofas, while KPI is still clean today: 0 late orders, 0 late sofas, 0 unplanned-late notices, 0 shortages.

# Inputs
- ERP overview on 2026-10-05: 26 sales orders, 18 planned orders, 8 unplanned orders (SO-2301..SO-2308), KPI all zero for lateness/shortages.
- CRM demand trend: baseline 1800 sofas vs 970 confirmed unplanned sofas, intake 54% above plan, Herbstzauber active at 100% daily budget until 2026-10-31.
- Unplanned orders are split across C-06, C-04, C-02, C-05 and C-03; the tier-A orders among them are SO-2303 and SO-2304.
- Factory capacity is currently 40 sofas/day at both F-NORTH and F-SOUTH for the next 10 workdays; no current production orders are late.
- Material projections show no shortage within 70 workdays for BEAM-PINE-80, FAB-OAT-01, or FAB-ANTH-02, so material is not the immediate bottleneck.
- Wiki: `protocols/handoffs.md` and `protocols/ordered-delegation.md` say to give colleagues ids, quantities, dates, and to chain dependent work in one step; `rules/capacity-levers.md` says to compare capacity levers by KPI and use overtime/temp workers only as needed; `rules/customer-notices.md` says notices only for orders late in ERP and to start with tier-A customers.
- Wiki read: `index.md`, `log.md`, `protocols/handoffs.md`, `protocols/ordered-delegation.md`, `rules/capacity-levers.md`, `rules/customer-notices.md`, `suppliers/overview.md`, `company/overview.md`.

# Steps
1. Ask Cora to re-plan the 8 unplanned sales orders into production orders with the existing factory split and priorities that protect tier-A orders first; include the exact order ids SO-2301..SO-2308 and ask her to return the new expected completion/delivery dates and any orders still late.
2. Ask Max to secure extra production capacity for both factories for the period needed by the new demand, using the smallest effective mix of overtime and temporary workers. The working assumption from the capacity rules is to prefer overtime for near-term gaps and temp workers only if needed; I have not yet fixed the exact package because the simulator did not expose nonzero outputs for the read-only checks.
3. Ask Lara to secure material only if Cora or Max identifies a real shortage after replanning; the current projections do not show a shortage, so this is a contingent follow-up rather than a default action.
4. Throttle Herbstzauber rather than stopping it: reduce the daily budget to 50% but keep the campaign active so at least half the current pace remains.
5. Recheck ERP KPI after the planning/capacity actions. If any order becomes late, then send customer notices only for orders whose ERP expected delivery date is after the promised date, starting with tier-A customers and using the ERP date only.

# Outputs
- `.agent/plans/task-01M61DGAK6MTH21QM2205YRV0J.md`
- `.agent/summaries/task-01M61DGAK6MTH21QM2205YRV0J_plan_1.md`

# Risks and open questions
- The simulator did not accept `update_campaign`, so the exact budget percentage for Herbstzauber still needs to be chosen in execute from the live CRM tool.
- The simulator did not produce meaningful nonzero capacity results for the production levers, so the exact capacity package still needs to be checked against live ERP execution.
- The current ERP KPI is clean, so the main risk is introducing unnecessary cost or changing the campaign too aggressively.
- We still need to confirm, in execute, whether the 8 unplanned orders can be planned without creating any late deliveries before any customer notice is sent.
